The most serious crime he can be convicted of is **C. Involuntary manslaughter**: transferred intent carries his intent to commit a battery over to the teammate's death, but intending only a slight wound does not supply the malice needed for murder, and there was no provocation for voluntary manslaughter. The shared note is wrong to call this mere negligence, because he deliberately fired a gun in an unlawful battery, so liability rests on the unlawful-act doctrine rather than carelessness.

CONFIDENCE: 70
